description:
Follow-ups from the ShortcutColumn port (src/columns/shortcut.rs, ported 2026-08-11 from DWSIM ShortcutColumn.vb @ 1abf72d1b6b41d3e9a8cc770d3cc4e8fc76e5766, 9/9 tests green in release, Android check clean).

1. PropertyPackageModel has no one-composition K-value form. Upstream calls DW_CalcKvalue(z, T, P) (ShortcutColumn.vb:201); the port approximates it with ColumnThermo::k_values(z, z, T, P) — exact for Ideal, first-order for cubics. Add a K(z, T, P) entry to the package enum and switch the shortcut (and any future caller) to it.

2. Mixture liquid density (upstream AUX_LIQDENS Rackett route, PropertyPackage.vb:7674) is implemented inline in the shortcut sizing block via Kay's-rule pseudo-criticals into petroleum::aux_props::liquid_density_rackett. Promote a package-level liquid-density entry into crate::thermo so shortcut sizing, pump NPSH inputs, etc. share one implementation.

3. (Optional, NOT upstream) Kirkbride feed-stage correlation as an alternative to the ported Fenske-ratio method — only if a design comparison is wanted; the port is deliberately faithful to upstream, which uses the Fenske ratio (ShortcutColumn.vb:512-519).
title: shortcut column follow-ups: one-composition K-value entry + promote mixture liquid density

description:
FIXED 2026-08-13 in outram-foam-basic-lib and in both vendored openfoam_source trees. RE-FILED because the original bead was LOST by the tracker after bn close reported success -- see docs/kopitiam-issues/kopi-beans-daemon-sync-fails-slotmap-too-small.md, UPDATE 2026-08-13.

DEFECT: normalize_error folded per-equation errors with .fold(0.0_f64, f64::max). Rust f64::max follows IEEE-754 maxNum and DISCARDS a NaN operand, so max(0.0, NaN) == 0.0. A NaN error read as ZERO error, the accept test err <= 1.0 passed immediately, and integrate returned Ok(()) with a NaN state. Affected Euler, Rkf45 and Rosenbrock23.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX FAILS: returning NaN does not work either, because the accept test is err <= 1.0 and every comparison against NaN is false -- the step is rejected but dx grinds to StepSizeUnderflow, naming the wrong cause.

FIX: the fold yields f64::INFINITY for a non-finite component; a new OdeError::NonFiniteState variant; an explicit !err.is_finite() guard in adaptive_step AND in Rosenbrock23, which duplicates that retry loop rather than calling the shared one. The enum variant was chosen over a wildcard so the compiler would find consumers -- in basic-lib it found offbeat viscochab building a state from a NaN result and returning it as success.

Demonstrated before fixing, both vendored trees printing identically: Euler/Rkf45/Rosenbrock23 all -> Ok(()), y = [NaN].
title: ode::normalize_error folds with f64::max, which discards NaN -- solver returned Ok(()) with a NaN state (FIXED)

description:
OUTSIDE THE SCOPE OF THE MELTING TASK -- reported, not fixed, because pimple_foam is verified against icoFoam reference fields and should not be touched without re-running that validation.

In crates/outram-foam-appbuilder-lib/src/solvers/pimple_foam/mod.rs, the PISO corrector updates only INTERNAL face fluxes:
    for f in 0..mesh.n_internal_faces { phi_hbya.internal[f] -= ...; }
    self.phi = phi_hbya;
The BOUNDARY values of self.phi keep whatever fvc::flux(&hbya) produced -- a zero-gradient extrapolation of HbyA, which is NOT zero at a no-slip wall. OpenFOAM constrains these (constrainHbyA / phi.boundaryFieldRef()).

Harmless in pimple_foam today because it transports no scalar: the momentum equation never reads phi.boundary. It becomes a real bug the moment any scalar transport is added, because fvm::div DOES read phi.boundary -- a spurious inward flux on a FixedValue patch enters as source -= phi_f*value.

Measured in melt_foam before the fix was added there: temperatures reached 362.93 K in a cavity whose hottest boundary was 311 K. The fix is the loop now in melt_foam::step (set phi.boundary[pi].values[fi] = u.boundary[pi].values[fi].dot(face_area_vectors[gf]), skipping Empty patches).

Suggested: port the same constraint into pimple_foam and re-run tutorials/pimple_foam_cavity.rs to confirm the icoFoam comparison is unchanged.

---
RE-FILED 2026-08-12 with its original id. This bead was created in an earlier session but never published, because beads-rs `bd` could not push the store ref (kopitiam#19). It survived only in the local v1 store, which diverged from origin's migrated v2 store. Preserved at ref refs/beads/local-preserve-20260812. Original status at preservation: open.
title: pimple_foam: phi boundary face fluxes are unconstrained after the PISO corrector

description:
THIS IS THE HTR-10 PASSIVE SAFETY CASE and there is no model of it. The scoping doc recommends budgeting for it rather than deferring it indefinitely, because it is the thing that makes the reactor worth simulating.

SCOPE: the heat removal route from bed to reflector to core barrel to reactor pressure vessel to the reactor cavity cooling system, by conduction and radiation, with no forced flow. This is what carries decay heat out during a loss of forced cooling without scram, and it is what the safety demonstration tests actually exercise.

Depends on graphite properties and bed effective conductivity — every temperature in this path is set by those two closures.

Also requires trustworthy decay heat, which is currently a separate defect — see the decay-heat bead.
title: HTR-10: reflector, core barrel and cavity-cooling decay-heat path
